rudimentary

roo-duh-MEN-tuh-ree -- stress on the third syllable, MEN. · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Rudimentary is primitive, basic, or undeveloped.

Using only a rudimentary raft of logs and rope, the explorers drifted forty miles downriver.

Example

The first airplane the brothers build is rudimentary: little more than a kite with a lawnmower engine -- no instruments, no seat belts, barely a seat.

That first flying machine is a basic, undeveloped early version of what airplanes would become. Rudimentary describes things at the crude first stage: functional, perhaps, but primitive and unrefined.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

elementary: Elementary means dealing with the first, simplest principles of a subject -- elementary arithmetic, an elementary mistake in logic. It describes where something sits in a course of learning, while rudimentary describes how undeveloped the thing itself is: a rudimentary tool simply has not been developed any further.

crude: Crude means rough and unrefined in how it is made -- a crude sketch, a crude shelter of branches. Crude judges workmanship, while rudimentary judges the stage of development: a rudimentary radio is early and simple, but a crude one is merely put together badly, whatever its era.

makeshift: Makeshift means improvised on the spot as a temporary substitute -- a makeshift bandage torn from a shirt. A makeshift thing is meant to be replaced soon, while a rudimentary thing may be simple yet permanent: a rudimentary alarm system can guard a shop for years.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

advanced: highly developed

sophisticated: complex and refined

Where it sits · how crude and early it is — basic → rudimentary → primitive

basic vs. rudimentary: Basic is gentler than rudimentary -- basic tools simply lack extras, while rudimentary tools are one step above nothing: crude, early, and unrefined.

primitive vs. rudimentary: Primitive goes further than rudimentary: a rudimentary radio is simple but works, while a primitive one belongs to the very dawn of the technology, barely recognizable next to the modern thing.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — rudi-

root — rudi-: rough, raw, unworked (Latin rudis)

suffix — -ment

suffix — -ment: result or means of (Latin -mentum)

suffix — -ary

suffix — -ary: relating to (Latin -arius)

Put it together

Put it together: Rudimentary builds on Latin rudis, 'rough, raw, unworked' -- the word Romans used for untrained recruits and unshaped stone. A rudimentum was a 'first attempt,' and something rudimentary is still in that rough first stage: the unpolished beginning of what it might one day become.

Root Check

Word Choice

Rudimentary pairs with knowledge, skills, tools, and systems: a rudimentary understanding of chemistry, rudimentary first-aid skills, a rudimentary alarm system. It is matter-of-fact rather than insulting -- calling your own French rudimentary is honest modesty, not self-mockery.
